This contradicts the key's uniform, single-colour, no-second-phase characterization.
o2.F4a+F4b+F4c.judge_why: All three crops (F4a, F4b, F4c) show red/black etched optical micrographs with dense, textured acicular/lath (Widmanstätten-type) microstructure and visible black interstitial regions between red laths, not a single uniform indexed colour with zero second-phase pixels; F4c additionally shows two labeled zones separated by a marked interface line. This is inconsistent with the node's claim of featureless single-colour phase maps with no second-phase pixels.

o3.F5a+F5b+F5c.why: WRONG: The candidate's description of the panel labeled BZ(C) (irregular, equiaxed grains with no directional trend) agrees with the key's "BZ grains are irregular and near-equiaxed." The panel labeled DZ(C) description (mosaic of irregularly shaped grains, some larger clustered, some finer equiaxed) does not clearly mention the key's "mixes elongated and blocky grains" feature — this is a partial miss but not a contradiction. However, the panel showing the interface/DZ(I) region is described as having "finer, more equiaxed grains in the DZ (I) region" (contrasted with large elongated grains on the HAZ side) — this directly contradicts the answer key, which states DZ(I) shows "long columnar grains rising steeply from the interface." Because one of the three panel descriptions contradicts the key's stated feature for that region, the overall candidate answer is graded WRONG.
o3.F5a+F5b+F5c.judge_why: All three crops show EBSD IPF orientation maps consistent with the node: F5a (BZ(C)) shows irregular, near-equiaxed interlocking grains with no directional bias; F5b (DZ(C)) shows a mix of large elongated reddish/orange grains alongside smaller blocky polygonal grains; F5c shows the HAZ(S)/Interface/DZ(I) transition where the DZ(I) side (right of the diagonal dashed interface line) contains elongated, columnar-shaped grains oriented steeply away from the interface, matching the node's claim. The second reader's description of DZ(I) as 'finer, more equiaxed' is a missed feature (the columnar grains are actually present in that region), not a case where the crop itself contradicts or fails to show what the node states -- so per the rubric this is a reader error, not a real citation error.

o5.F2a+F2b+F2c.why: WRONG — The answer key states these are pattern-quality maps (a technique such as EBSD-derived band-contrast/pattern-quality imaging) where BZ(C) shows the finest lath contrast while DZ(C) and DZ(I) show coarser blocks and longer laths. The candidate instead identifies all three panels as optical (light) etched micrographs of martensitic/bainitic/Widmanstätten lath structures, misattributing the imaging technique, and describes all three panels similarly as fine, dense, acicular microstructures without capturing the key's fine-vs-coarse comparative distinction between panels. This constitutes a technique mismatch and a failure to reflect the key's central comparative feature, so it is graded WRONG rather than merely PARTIAL.
o5.F2a+F2b+F2c.judge_why: All three crops show etched lath/acicular microstructure micrographs with a scale bar, and comparing them shows panel (a) with the densest, finest crisscrossing lath network while (b) and (c) show visibly coarser, larger block-like lath/grain colonies and longer plate features, consistent with node o5's fine-vs-coarse comparison. The reader's 'optical light micrograph' label versus the key's 'pattern-quality map' (EBSD band-contrast) is an instrument/technique-naming difference that needs text to resolve, not a contradiction of what the crop visually shows, so per the instrument-fact rule this is ok rather than real.

o6.F7.why: CORRECT: the candidate's chart matches the key's grain-size distribution comparison, noting BZ truncating near ~17-18 µm (close to the key's ~17.5 µm) and DZ/DZ(I) tails extending to ~20-24 µm (matching the key's ~24 µm), with no contradictory claims.

o13.F11.why: CORRECT: The candidate's description matches the key. It identifies the same numeric extremes (tensile up to 555 at top, compressive down to -1005 near the middle depth) and the same overall trend — tensile near the top surface, falling to compressive around 1100-1300 μm (consistent with the key's -810 to -1005 near 1200 μm), then recovering toward tensile/neutral deeper in the HAZ (consistent with the key's "positive again below ~1450 μm"). No contradiction with the key's feature or trend.

a2.F11.why: PARTIAL: The candidate describes a residual-stress (RS) heat map with three zones (Bead Zone, Dilution/DZ, HAZ) and reports spatial trends that are broadly compatible with the key (tensile in BZ, compressive in DZ, recovering toward tensile in HAZ). However, the answer key's actual claim is about an IQ-RS inversion — image quality (IQ) rising as RS falls in BZ, falling as RS turns tensile in HAZ, and falling in DZ as RS turns more compressive. The candidate's description never mentions IQ or any inverse relationship between two variables; it only describes the RS map alone. Since it doesn't mention this key feature but doesn't contradict the RS trends either, this is a PARTIAL match per the grading note (candidate omits the key's central comparison without contradicting the underlying RS trends).
